top_choice_rationale: P001 awards Katori and Ye for the invention and realisation of the optical lattice clock. The magic-wavelength condition is a distinct physical idea that removes the dominant systematic of trapped-atom clocks and allows many atoms to be interrogated at once, which underlies the 1e-18 uncertainty. Delivered results include the gravitational redshift resolved across millimetre-scale height differences and clock-comparison bounds on constant variation. The work is mature and the two-name allocation is defensible, though precision-measurement cumulative weight and omitted contributors are real limits. That is a case for careful citation wording, not for withholding the prize, so no award ranks last.
